title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this and the neighbouring pages:
- 𝔊^+ is a profinite group of 'modular' type, probably a profinite completion of SL(2,Z) or a variant. It has distinguished torsion elements ρ and σ, whose procyclic subgroups L_ρ and L_σ both contain {±1}.
- L_0 is a procyclic 'loop' or inertia subgroup, apparently attached to a cusp, and L_1 = ρ L_0 ρ^{-1} is its transform under conjugation by ρ.
- Z_{ρ,σ} is the group of quadruples (u, μ, ε, ε') with u ∈ Aut(𝔊^+), μ ∈ Ẑ^* and ε, ε' ∈ {±1}, subject to the conditions (6) of an earlier page. These presumably say:
  - u(ρ) is conjugate to ρ^ε and u(σ) is conjugate to σ^{ε'};
  - u acts on L_0 by the power μ, i.e. u(ℓ) = ℓ^μ, with u normalised at the 'cusp' L_0.
- The previous page shows that if 𝔊^+ is 'big enough' (for example if it maps to GL(2,Ẑ) in a modular way), then (μ, ε, ε') is determined by u. So Z_{ρ,σ} embeds in Aut(𝔊^+).

This page:
- (13) Each ℓ ∈ L_0 gives (int(ℓ), 1, 1, 1) ∈ Z_{ρ,σ}. This makes sense because inner automorphisms preserve conjugacy classes and L_0 is abelian, so int(ℓ) is the identity on L_0. The image is normal ('invariante'). The kernel is L_0 ∩ Cent(𝔊^+), i.e. L_0 intersected with the centre.
- (14) L_0 ∩ Centre ⊂ L_0 ∩ Cent_{𝔊^+}(ρ) ⊂ L_0 ∩ L_1. Reason: if ℓ commutes with ρ then ℓ = ρℓρ^{-1} ∈ ρ L_0 ρ^{-1} = L_1.
- If L_0 ∩ L_1 = {1}, the kernel is trivial (15). This holds when there is a map to GL(2,Ẑ) that is injective on L_0, since the unipotent subgroups of two distinct cusps meet trivially. Grothendieck assumes this from now on.
- (16)-(17) He defines Γ_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}/Im L_0, giving an exact sequence 1 → L_0 → Z_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1. The projections to μ, ε, ε' are trivial on Im L_0, so they factor through Γ, giving characters χ_Γ, ε_Γ, ε'_Γ to Ẑ^* × {±1} × {±1}.
- Purpose: to build a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group Γ_{ρ,σ}. It consists of automorphisms of the profinite modular group that preserve the conjugacy classes of the elliptic generators up to sign, normalised at a cusp, taken modulo the residual inner action of the cusp group, with a cyclotomic character χ. The next page then forms the semidirect products Z_{ρ,σ}·𝔊^+ (and S_0G_{ρ,σ}, G_{ρ,σ}), which serve as candidate 'arithmetic' fundamental groups for the solutions of the 'équation des lacets'.
errors: (14) is written with '=' between L_0 ∩ Cent_{𝔊^+}(ρ) and L_0 ∩ L_1. The argument only proves the inclusion ⊂, and only the inclusion is needed.

The logic of 'a fortiori s'il existe seulement (12')' is loose. What is really needed is that some quotient map is injective on L_0 and separates L_0 from L_1. Note also that (12') is written for 𝔊 rather than 𝔊^+; this is minor.

The claim that the image of (13) is normal implicitly uses the normalisation u|_{L_0} = (power μ) in the definition of Z, i.e. u(ℓ) = ℓ^μ exactly rather than up to conjugacy. This is consistent but not restated on this page.

ideas.what: Group Z_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms of the profinite modular group preserving the conjugacy classes of the elliptic elements ρ and σ up to sign, acting by a cyclotomic power on a cusp subgroup L_0
ideas.modern_name: normalised / 'special' automorphisms of profinite SL2(Z) or braid-type groups; Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura for automorphisms of profinite modular/braid groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the Teichmüller tower and SL2(Z) philosophy, but not these explicit groups

ideas.what: Embedding of the cusp group L_0 via inner automorphisms, with kernel L_0 ∩ centre; triviality shown via L_0 ∩ ρL_0ρ^{-1} = 1
ideas.modern_name: inner automorphisms by inertia / tangential base point ambiguity

ideas.what: Quotient Γ_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}/L_0 with characters χ (cyclotomic) and ε, ε' (signs)
ideas.modern_name: GT-like group with cyclotomic character, analogous to GT̂ → Ẑ^*

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a 'modular' GT-type group Γ_{ρ,σ} attached to a pair of elliptic elements of a profinite group 𝔊^+. Its definition is relative to an arbitrary 'big enough' quotient 𝔊 (a family of groups, not only Ŝl2(Z)). It carries the extra sign characters ε, ε' alongside the cyclotomic one. This is a mild variant of known constructions (automorphisms of profinite SL2(Z) / PSL2(Z) preserving elliptic classes). Whether this relative-to-𝔊 family has been studied systematically is unclear, but it is probably not significantly new.
missed.quote: On pose (16) Γ_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ} / Im L_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possible comparison point with the work of Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and Minamide–Nakamura on automorphisms of profinite modular and braid groups. Any novelty is minor.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful set-up of a GT-type automorphism group for a profinite modular group: an exact sequence and the characters. The mathematics is routine and close in spirit to well-known later work (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura), with no new result on the page.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'connaissance de u ∈ Aut(𝔊^+)', not Aut(Ĝ^+). Similarly, read 𝔊^+ for Ĝ^+ in (14)-(15).
'dont l'image est invariante, le noyau n'étant autre que L_0 ∩ Cent(𝔊^+)'.
Projection line: '(u, μ, ε, ε') ↦ μ, ε, ε'' — read ε, not ξ.
'Γ_{ρ,σ}' (capital Gamma, as on the next page), not 'γ_{ρ,σ}'.
The word after (12') is uncertain; it might be 'unilatère' or 'injectif'.
